extracted.intended_audience: NIH scientific grant reviewers and NIH grant applicants (RPG programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard definitions and guidance for critiquing RPG (Research Project Grant) applications for NIH review panels, including overall impact and the core scored criteria plus special considerations for specific grant mechanisms and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (all RPG Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering all of the review criteria, briefly summarize the significant strengths and weaknesses of the application and state the likelihood of the project to exert a sustained powerful influence on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise summary of the most important strengths and weaknesses and an overall judgment about the project's potential to have a sustained, powerful influence. Applicable to all RPG applications; other mechanism-specific guidance (R03, R15, R21) may modify expectations for breadth/detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant Program) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because R03 projects are limited, applications may not contain extensive detail; reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can come from literature citations, external data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot/feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (Academic Research Enhancement Award - AREA) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the proposed project addresses AREA objectives: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen research environment of schools not major NIH recipients, (3) expose undergraduate/graduate students to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess overall impact with respect to AREA program goals. Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant Program) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact. R21 need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Appropriate justification can include literature citations, other-source data, or investigator-generated data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the importance of the problem, potential to advance the field, and the magnitude of the impact if aims are met. Consider effect on concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience/training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that advanced their field(s)? For multi-PD/PI, do investigators have complementary and integrated expertise and appropriate leadership/governance/organizational structure?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess qualifications, track record, appropriateness of team composition, and leadership/organizational plans for collaborative projects. Consider special evaluation for ESI/NI status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions? Are the concepts/approaches/instrumentation novel to one field or novel in a broad sense? Is a refinement, improvement, or new application proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge degree of novelty and paradigm-shifting potential, or whether the project is an incremental refinement. Consider novelty within and across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage risky aspects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rigor, feasibility, identification of risks/alternatives, and milestones. For clinical research, also evaluate plans for human subjects protection and inclusion of minorities, sexes/genders, and children (see Human Subjects/Inclusion sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate? Will the project benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional/infrastructure support, access to resources and populations, and whether unique environment adds substantive value to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (non-exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects that is not exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate justification for involvement and proposed protections according to five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether human subjects are appropriately justified and protected relative to scientific goals. For clinical trials, pay attention to data and safety monitoring plans. These five criteria form the basis for human subjects evaluation; significant weaknesses here affect overall impact and approach scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (exempt research considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that meets criteria for one or more of the six exempt categories under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate: (1) the justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when claiming exemption, applicants must justify that exemption is appropriate and describe subject involvement and material sources; reviewers will judge adequacy of these justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion of minorities and members of both genders, as well as the inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess appropriateness and justification of inclusion plans relative to scientific goals and research strategy. Lack of adequate inclusion plans can be a substantive weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: (1) proposed use and species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; (2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures to limit discomfort/distress/pain including use of analgesia/anesthesia and restraint; (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should determine whether animal use is justified, humane, and scientifically appropriate; evaluate care and pain-minimization procedures and euthanasia methods with reference to standards (AVMA Guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment, and whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider biosafety, containment, training, and mitigation plans. Inadequate biosafety protections are a substantive concern and can affect funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Resubmission application (formerly amended), the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review updated application content and judge whether prior concerns were adequately addressed and whether revisions materially improved the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Renewal application (formerly competing continuation), the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prior progress, productivity, outcomes, and how past performance supports continuation of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Revision application (formerly competing supplement), the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project. If the Revision relates to a line of investigation from the original application that was not recommended, the committee will consider whether responses to previous comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed revisions are justified, responsive to prior critiques, and represent meaningful and appropriate expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess realism and justification of costs and duration. Over- or under-funded budgets or unjustified timeframes are weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess information provided about Select Agent(s), including: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with select agent regulations and adequacy of biosafety/biocontainment/security plans. Missing or insufficient plans are serious deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether foreign-based resources or settings offer unique scientific advantages and whether these justify funding relative to U.S.-based alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable for: (1) Data Sharing Plan; (2) Sharing Model Organisms; and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the reasonableness and feasibility of data/model organism/GWAS sharing plans or rationales for why sharing is not possible. Links and NIH policy references provide further expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-text opportunity for reviewers to give constructive feedback, advise on improvements, or state that resubmission would require major changes; such comments inform applicants beyond numeric scores.
